title: Incident Contextualizer: automated trace/log snapshots + Slack / PagerDuty action buttons
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Summary:
Build an automated Incident Contextualizer service that enriches PagerDuty incidents and Slack alert threads with pre-computed context: a concise trace/span snippet, top-5 correlated log lines, metric mini-sparkshots (latency/error rate +/- 5m), and an error fingerprint. The enriched payload should attach a one-click Runbook action (Slack buttons + PD links) that can: 1) execute the curated runbook flow, 2) create a skeleton postmortem draft (timeline + metric snapshots), or 3) trigger a limited scoped reroute/fallback policy.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-context for on-call by 60% (measure by median time to first-diagnostic comment).
- Ensure context payload is compact (<= 1200 bytes for Slack PD payloads after encoding) and respects PII stripping rules.
- Make the runbook action idempotent and auditable (logs of who triggered, when, and result).

Scope:
- Server-side enrichment service that listens to alerts and incident-create hooks from the observability pipeline.
- Query short-lived trace store for top N spans around the alert timestamp and synthesize a 3-4 line human-readable snippet.
- Pull top correlated logs (based on trace id and error scores) and redact PII before inclusion.
- Capture small metric windows (latency p50/p90/p99, error rate) as tiny sparkline PNGs or ASCII sparklines embedded in Slack where available.
- Add Slack action buttons (Runbook, Create Postmortem Draft, Trigger Fallback) with secure one-time tokens.
- PD enrichment via PD event API attachments and incident notes.
- Postmortem skeleton generator that populates a Confluence/Drive template with timeline placeholders and metric snapshots for the incident lead to fill in.

Non-Goals:
- Full automated remediation (beyond firing a controlled fallback API).
- Long-term storage of raw logs or traces (we re-query short-lived stores and only store derived summaries).
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment payload attached to PD incidents and top-level Slack threads for simulated alerts
Trace snippet shows highlighted suspect spans and matches ground-truth from 2 curated incidents
Logs included are top-5 correlated lines with PII redaction verified by Security
Slack action buttons call back to secure endpoints and perform the documented flows
Postmortem skeleton is created in Drive/Confluence with timeline and metric snapshots
Payload size stays below 1200 bytes (or gracefully degrades to a link if exceeded)
comments: 2025-03-02 Priya Raman: Initial ticket created after Ops tabletop on 2025-02-27. Problem: on-call spends too long assembling traces/logs during P0s. Proposed prototype: server-side summarizer + action buttons.

2025-03-04 Ethan Morales: Spike complete — proof-of-concept pulls traces via trace-store v2, extracts top spans by error-score, and generates a 3-line summary. Found performance hotpath: querying trace-store for high-cardinality services takes ~400ms per request. Suggest caching common service schemas for 10m.

2025-03-05 Sofia Kim (Design): Reviewed Slack message UX — recommended an abbreviated header and expandable attachment with 'Show full context' link to avoid noisy threads. Also suggested one-click acknowledgement vs. runbook flows split to avoid accidental triggers.

2025-03-06 Security review note (Anand Patel): PII redaction required for logs and trace tags. Must use existing redaction library (redwood-redact v1.2) and add an allowlist for engineers. Also require audit log entry for any runbook actions.

2025-03-08 Engineering sync: Decided to implement action tokens as short-lived JWTs signed by ops-keyring, validated by contextor service. Trade-off: slight latency for token minting (~12ms) vs much simpler security model. Agreed to batch token mint for multi-button payloads.

2025-03-10 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821 — scaffolds contextor service, trace snippet extraction, and Slack attachment formatter. Needs review on redaction integration and unit tests for PII edge cases.

2025-03-11 QA note (Maya Lopez): Ran integration tests with staging PD/Slack. Slack UI looks clean, but attachments occasionally hit the 8KB payload limit when including 5 logs + sparkline PNG. Plan: switch to link-to-diff view for >3 logs or include ASCII sparkline instead of PNG.

2025-03-12 Ethan Morales: Iterating on PR per feedback. Next steps: add Confluence template integration, ensure PD attachments use compact JSON and fallback to link if payload > 1200 bytes, add e2e test simulating P0 traffic.
work_log: 2025-03-03 Spike: trace-store query patterns and latency profiling (Ethan)
2025-03-05 UX pass: Slack + PD attachment design (Sofia)
2025-03-08 Implementation: contextor service scaffold, token generation (Ethan)
notes: Implementation detail: to avoid extra latency, contextor will sample traces and compute summaries asynchronously; the initial PD/Slack incident is created immediately and then updated with enrichment within 8s. If enrichment fails, we post a note linking to the enrichment retry queue.
Observability: add metrics for enrichment_success_rate, enrichment_latency_ms, payload_size_bytes; create alert if success_rate < 95% over 5m.
Rollout plan: beta with internal on-call team for 2 weeks, then expand to broader infra teams. Provide opt-out per-service via metadata tag 'ops.contextualizer=disabled'.
